Hi Jasmine,

We started seeing large QPS variance across pods in our private VPC cluster this morning around 08:30 PDT. P95 for inference rose from ~220ms to ~1.2s intermittently; we also saw a burst of 502s for ~12 minutes at 08:45. This is impacting our API consumers.

We collected a short span of logs and a heap dump — attaching the zip. We suspect something is causing KV cache churn or a decode stall when some requests include long context windows.

Can Redwood confirm whether any config changes or background jobs ran on your side? We have not rolled any internal changes.

Attaching: svc-logs-zenith-20260805.zip

Thanks,

> We’ll aim for a short conference call in 30 minutes to walk through the traces. Marcus, Laura — looping you for a quick look.

Downloaded the logs. Quick observations:
- Multiple workers reporting KV cache eviction churn coincident with p95 spikes — i.e., sustained cache misses for hot prefixes.
- Decoder failed requests correlate to nodes that hit sudden CPU steal (host-level) around 08:44.
- A subset of requests include longer prompt lengths (~1.8x of baseline) which increases decoding windows and may expose kernel inefficiencies on older GPU drivers.

Immediate mitigations we can propose:
1) Toggle temporary routing to the dedicated fallback pool for high-priority routes (buy us ~60s of headroom).
2) Increase K/V cache size on the affected node group (config change, quick restart needed).
3) If agreed, warm a short-lived burst of capacity in the private cluster to offload peak traffic.

I’ll attach a heap profile I pulled from the node and a short ops checklist.

Quick internal update and proposed MAP (mutual action plan):

Summary of root triggers (early hypothesis):
- Workload variance: increased prompt sizes + periodic batch jobs that puncture warm caches.
- Cache evictions causing repeated cold decode + queued kernel scheduling pressure on older GPU nodes.
- A small number of hosts showing host-level CPU steal (noisy neighbor).

Proposed short-term runbook (0–3 hours):
- Approve temporary routing to fallback pool (Jasmine to confirm with Zenith ops).
- Increase KV cache allocation on affected node group; rolling restart of 2 nodes at a time.
- Apply minor decoder parameter tweak (reduce per-request parallelism) that has been safe in prior incidents.
- Monitor p95 and 502 rate for 30-minute windows after change.

Longer-term (3–72 hours):
- Upgrade GPU driver on nodes flagged for steal.
- Tune kernel selection to prefer the lower-latency path for high-variance inputs.
- Add a living prompt-length histogram to telemetry for customer-owned clusters.

Priyom, can you draft the MAP doc and send to Anika/Marco with proposed windows for rolling restarts? Need explicit go/no-go criteria from Zenith for the restart + temporary burst.

Laura Bennett
Director, Private Deployments
